answer.rationale: memory_c2 describes the last time we cut unit cost by moving primary supply to a new vendor. Finance mandates an 18% spend reduction this cycle and the incumbent has refused to reprice. The primary contract also expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so a switch is mechanically possible. The assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, which raises delivery risk on a vendor change; that risk is the main thing I want the source record to clarify. memory_c2 is the closest analogue - successful onboarding with a low-cost vendor - so verifying it confirms whether the speed and stability of that transition actually held, or whether onboarding pressure showed up later. If it holds, switch_primary_vendor is the only move that plausibly hits the 18% target given the incumbent's refusal; the other directions either leave cost flat (renew_incumbent, defer_decision) or only partially address it while adding integration complexity in a no-buffer window (add_second_source, negotiate_terms). Renewing the incumbent or deferring would fail the primary objective. Adding a second source or negotiating terms cannot by themselves close an 18% gap when the incumbent has refused to move. A switch carries delivery risk in a tight volume window, so the verification budget is spent on the memory most likely to confirm or refute that the low-cost vendor path can be executed quickly enough not to disturb the 94% utilization line.
